questions.q: What is a point of view (POV) in the context of running a Financial Reporting Studio report?
options: A written opinion attached to the report
The specific slice of the GL balances cube to report on, such as ledger, period, and scenario
A setting that changes the report's row and column design permanently
A security role assigned to the report
questions.explain: The report design (rows, columns, formulas) stays fixed; the point of view tells it which specific slice of data — ledger, period, scenario, currency — to pull each time it runs.

questions.q: Which of these is typically part of a report's point of view?
options: The font used in the Financial Reporting Web Studio editor
Ledger, period, and scenario
The user's job title
The name of the Oracle data center
questions.explain: Common POV dimensions include ledger, accounting period, scenario (Actual, Budget, Forecast), and sometimes currency.

questions.q: What is a typical reason to export a seeded financial report to PDF or Excel rather than only viewing it online?
options: Online viewing is not possible for seeded reports
Sharing outside the system or archiving the exact result from a specific period, such as for a close binder
Exporting is required before a report can even be run
PDF exports automatically update every day
questions.explain: Exporting preserves a point-in-time result for distribution or archiving, while online viewing supports interactive review and drill.

questions.q: A seeded report shows numbers that look wrong. What should be checked FIRST, before assuming the report design itself is broken?
options: Immediately rebuild the entire report from scratch
The point of view that was selected when the report ran
The font size used in the output
Whether BI Publisher is installed
questions.explain: A report run against an unexpected point of view, such as the wrong period or ledger, will look wrong while actually being correct for what it was given.

questions.q: After confirming the point of view is correct, what should be checked next if a report's numbers still seem off?
options: The user's data security / data access set scope
Whether the user has a favorite color set in their profile
The report's file name
Nothing further; the report design must be at fault
questions.explain: Data security can legitimately narrow the rows a user sees, so it's checked before assuming the underlying report design has a defect.
